At the same 25 dBA, the budget towers land within 2.4 to 3.8°C of Noctua's $150 NH-D15 G2. Data: GamersNexus. [...] GamersNexus tested the standard Peerless Assassin 120 on its 2025 AM5 bench. That is the non-SE model, also a dual tower with two 120mm fans. With a Ryzen 7 9800X3D pulling about 157W and the fans turned down to 25 dBA, it held 63.4°C over a 21°C room. That works out to about 84°C on the chip.

Noctua’s NH-D15 G2, which GamersNexus priced at $150, was only 2.4°C cooler in the same test. Treat the GamersNexus figure as a close guide to the SE, not a result for the SE itself. [...] The 9800X3D is a 120W chip with a 162W PPT, and AMD recommends a liquid cooler for it. GamersNexus’s 157W load is close to that limit, and there the standard Peerless Assassin 120 held about 84°C on the chip at 25 dBA. A dual tower works if you accept that. The FX360 Pro gives you about 7°C more headroom. For a Ryzen 9 9950X3D (170W, 230W PPT), go liquid. On GamersNexus’s overclocked 276W load, the FX360 Pro was the weakest AIO tested and ran warm unless its fans were turned up.
